bull_case: Clinically differentiated metabolic medicines address large unmet need, while oral and next-generation options broaden access. High gross margins and accelerating volume show strong product economics.
bear_case: Patient demand can be strong while payer economics deteriorate. Chronic adherence, reimbursement restrictions and lower realized prices can reduce lifetime value and limit usage.
thesis: Customer/product strength is high. Q2 volume rose 60% while gross margin reached 85.8%, showing strong demand and operating leverage despite lower realized prices. The products address mission-critical diabetes/obesity outcomes, but direct retention/adherence evidence is less complete than revenue evidence. Payers and governments are major economic customers, so lower realized pricing prevents a maximum customer-ROI score.

evidence.claim: Q2 revenue rose 48% as volume increased 60%, partially offset by a 13% decline in realized prices.
Q2 gross margin was $19.7B, or 85.8% of revenue, up 1.5 percentage points YoY despite lower realized prices.
Mounjaro revenue rose 91% YoY to $9.943B in Q2, with both U.S. and international volume expansion.
Zepbound revenue rose 46% YoY to $4.928B in Q2 despite lower realized prices, indicating strong patient/prescriber demand.
FDA approval of oral orforglipron for obesity adds a lower-friction form factor that can expand access beyond injections.

counterevidence: Q2 realized prices fell 13%, highlighting payer and reimbursement bargaining power.
Long-term adherence and persistence data are not captured by revenue growth alone.
Competing incretins may narrow efficacy and convenience differentiation.
Government reimbursement decisions can reduce economics even when clinical demand is strong.
unknowns: Long-run adherence/persistence by product and indication.
Net lifetime value after rebates and payer mix shifts.
falsifiers: Volume growth slows while realized pricing continues to decline sharply.
Successor products fail to improve access or adherence.
Gross-margin expansion reverses structurally as competition and rebates intensify.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Large volume growth, regulatory approvals and very high gross margins demonstrate clinically demanded products rather than subsidy-only growth.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 단일 제품·단일 고객·단일 규제에 대한 치명적 종속성
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Revenue is concentrated in metabolic therapy but spans multiple molecules, indications, geographies and other therapeutic areas; no single customer is existential.

key_kpis.name: Gross margin
key_kpis.threshold: remain structurally high despite capacity and pricing changes

key_kpis.name: Adherence / access
key_kpis.threshold: broader reimbursement and oral options expand durable use

subscores.rationale: The medicines address major health outcomes and demand is strong, but payer/reimbursement pressure means economic ROI is shared among patients, providers and payers rather than fully captured by Lilly.
Volume is expanding rapidly at scale, but direct same-cohort adherence/retention evidence is less complete than commercial usage evidence.
Q2 gross margin of 85.8% expanded despite lower realized pricing and large-scale volume growth, indicating powerful product economics.

uncertainties.rationale: Payer willingness to reimburse at scale is the binding economic customer question.
Commercial growth is clear but chronic persistence is less directly evidenced.
Current gross-margin economics are strongly evidenced.
